patch.value: presets commands redeclared host-owned --json global, failing registration on pm-cli 2026.7.27

pm-cli 2026.7.27 ships GH-719: the host rejects any extension command whose flags shadow a host-owned global flag. The presets package declared { long: "--json" } in a shared JSON_FLAG constant spread across presets list, presets show, presets diff, presets export, presets validate, and the bare presets command. Every one of these commands failed to register against a real pm host. The existing test suite used the SDK testing harness but had no suite-wide guard asserting the host-owned flag invariant. Fix: removed the --json flag from the JSON_FLAG constant (now empty), and changed the two handler reads of readBooleanOption(options, 'json') to ctx.global?.json === true. The --json flag still works because it is host-owned — pm accepts it and renders JSON output; the extension just must not redeclare it. Also fixed the audit:prod script which used plain 'npm audit --omit=dev' instead of the 'env -u npm_config_allow_scripts npm audit --omit=dev --ignore-scripts' form required by project-scoped installs. Removed the last 'as any' cast in registry.test.ts. Added a suite-wide guard test asserting no registered command redeclares any of the nine host-owned globals. Bumped pm-cli to 2026.7.27.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Verified: activation probe prints failed=[] against the real pm host engine. npm test: 47/47 pass including the new suite-wide guard test asserting no command redeclares any host-owned global. release:check green end to end (typecheck, build, test, audit:prod, pack:dry-run, changelog:check). The --json flag is read from ctx.global.json in the presets diff and presets --diff handlers. All usage examples mentioning --json remain valid since --json still works as a host-owned global.

patch.value: Presets commands re-register under pm-cli 2026.7.27 after dropping the shadowing --json declaration. Left unattributed on purpose: the release is pending, not cut, so --release-version-from-package places it correctly on its own.
Presets commands register successfully on pm-cli 2026.7.27, with the entry under the pending 2026.7.27 heading.

Before the fix, redeclaring the host-owned --json global aborted registration at that command and dropped every later sibling, while --help still exited 0 with a misleading arity error (upstream pm-cli#772).

Retired as shipped: the fix stopping presets commands from redeclaring the host-owned --json global merged as PR #32. Deliberately closed with NO release attribution because pm-presets has no v2026.07.27 tag yet -- 2026.7.27 is the PENDING release derived from package.json, so the entry lands there naturally without asserting it was in an already-cut release.

value.text: Correction: this item was briefly closed with no release attribution on the belief that no v2026.07.27 tag existed. That reading came from STALE LOCAL TAGS. After git fetch --tags --force the tag is present and git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the fix commit dcca13e is contained in v2026.07.27 -- the tag in fact points directly at it. Attributed to 2026.7.27 accordingly, so the entry sits with its siblings from the same release window instead of in Unreleased.
